Is Na Muang waterfall free? | Yes. There is no entry fee at Na Muang 1, and the signed left-hand path to Na Muang 2 is free. You pay only for parking: about 20 THB for a scooter and 60 THB for a car at the Na Muang 1 car park.
Can you swim at Na Muang 1? | Yes. The 18 m fall drops into a wide pool that is the best waterfall swim on Samui. The bottom shelves quickly and the depth changes through the year, so check before you jump and keep children close.
How long is the hike to Na Muang 2? | 20–40 minutes each way from the top car parks via the left-hand path and the wooden bridge, depending on fitness and how wet the rock is. Allow 1.5–3 hours for the visit, including a rest at the top.
Which Na Muang waterfall is better? | Na Muang 1 for swimming, families and an easy visit; Na Muang 2 for a steep climb and bigger views. Most visitors do Na Muang 1 and add Na Muang 2 only if they are fit and have grippy shoes.
When does Na Muang have the most water? | October to January, during and after the north-east monsoon; November is the wettest month at about 445 mm. Late December and January combine good flow with safer rock. From February to April both falls thin to a trickle.
Is Na Muang open in the rainy season? | Yes, both falls stay open, but after heavy rain the stream can rise quickly and turn brown and the Na Muang 2 trail becomes dangerous. On those days swim at Na Muang 1 only.
Can I get to Na Muang Waterfall without a scooter? | Yes: hire a car, take a taxi with an agreed return fare and waiting time, or join a 4x4 jungle safari that includes the swim. Grab can drop you off but is unreliable for the return, and there is no regular songthaew.
Is there an elephant camp at Na Muang? | Yes, there are elephant attractions on the road to the falls, and 2026 visitor reports describe elephants in cramped enclosures with rides still offered. We don't recommend any of them; park at the waterfall's own car park and see our sanctuary guide for no-riding options.
What are the Na Muang waterfall opening hours? | Na Muang 1 is listed as open 09:00–17:00 daily (some listings say from 08:00) and Na Muang 2 as 09:00–18:00. Hours can change on Thai public holidays; arrive at opening to beat the tour groups.
How high is Na Muang waterfall? | Na Muang 1 drops about 18 m into its pool. Na Muang 2 is the tallest on Samui, about 80 m in total over at least five tiers.
Are there toilets and food at Na Muang? | Yes. Na Muang 1 has toilets, food stalls, a café and souvenir shops between the car park and the pool. Na Muang 2 has toilets and a small café near the start of the trail; bring water for the climb.
How far is Na Muang from Lamai and Chaweng? | About 11 km (15–20 minutes) from Lamai and 20 km (30–40 minutes) from Chaweng, via Hua Thanon and the ring road, Route 4169. From Nathon it is about 12 km south.
